message.content:
## Decision

**Runner A (GOTOOLCHAIN=auto, go 1.21.0 + toolchain go1.21.9):** `auto` = `local+auto`, so the default toolchain is the bundled 1.21.3. Since the `toolchain go1.21.9` line is newer than the default, the go command runs go1.21.9 instead; finding no `go1.21.9` on PATH, it **downloads and verifies** that toolchain ([selection](https://go.dev/doc/toolchain#select), [download](https://go.dev/doc/toolchain#download)). It needs a working proxy/network plus the checksum database.

**Runner B (GOTOOLCHAIN=local, go 1.21.9):** `local` always runs the bundled toolchain, and since Go 1.21 a toolchain **refuses to load a module whose go line declares a newer version** — 1.21.3 exits with an error on a `go 1.21.9` module ([config](https://go.dev/doc/toolchain#config), [select](https://go.dev/doc/toolchain#select)).

**Runner C (GOTOOLCHAIN=go1.21.3+path):** the default is 1.21.3, but the `toolchain go1.21.9` line is newer, so it tries to run 1.21.9. `+path` disables the download fallback, so after scanning PATH (no go1.21.9), **it stops and fails** ([select](https://go.dev/doc/toolchain#select)).

## go vs toolchain directives

- `go` = the **mandatory minimum** Go version to use the module (since Go 1.21), sets the enforced language version, and must be ≥ every dependency's `go` line ([config](https://go.dev/doc/toolchain#config), [go directive](https://go.dev/doc/modules/gomod-ref#go)).
- `toolchain` = a **suggested** toolchain; it only takes effect when the module is the main module and the default toolchain is older ([toolchain directive](https://go.dev/doc/modules/gomod-ref#toolchain)).

A dependency's `toolchain` line has **no effect on downstream consumers** — only the main module's is consulted. But a dependency's `go` line does propagate: `go get`/`go mod tidy` raise the main module's `go` line to meet a new dependency's requirement, potentially forcing consumers onto a newer toolchain.

## Incorrect proposals

- **GOSUMDB=off:** backwards. Toolchain downloads are module-like and verified; with `GOSUMDB=off` they **fail for lack of verification**. GOPRIVATE/GONOSUMDB patterns don't apply to them ([download](https://go.dev/doc/toolchain#download)). For restricted CI, use an internal GOPROXY that serves `golang.org/toolchain` with GOSUMDB on (recommendation).
- **"+path makes the build network-free":** UNVERIFIED/false in scope. `+path` only disables the toolchain fallback; dependency fetches still honor GOPROXY and can hit the network.

## Policy (recommendation)

Pin CI runners with an explicit `GOTOOLCHAIN=<name>` or `local` matching the intended version; keep `go` lines as low as the code genuinely needs; treat `toolchain` as developer convenience, not a consumer contract.

**Not guaranteed:** a `toolchain` line in your published module will not lock consumers to that version; a `go 1.21.x` line guarantees the minimum and language version, not which patch build compiles consumers' code.

I have everything I need from the two pages. Let me reason through each runner.

Runner A: GOTOOLCHAIN=auto (=local+auto), bundled 1.21.3, module go 1.21.0 + toolchain go1.21.9. Default toolchain = local (1.21.3). toolchain line go1.21.9 is newer than 1.21.3 → switch to go1.21.9, search PATH (not found) → download and verify via checksum DB. Requires network/proxy; with GOSUMDB=off, toolchain downloads fail for lack of verification.

Runner B: GOTOOLCHAIN=local, module go 1.21.9. Bundled 1.21.3 refuses to load module declaring go 1.21.9 (newer). Error and exit.

Runner C: GOTOOLCHAIN=go1.21.3+path, module go 1.21.0 + toolchain go1.21.9, same PATH (no go1.21.9). Default toolchain is 1.21.3. toolchain line 1.21.9 is newer → runs 1.21.9 instead, searches PATH, not found; +path disables download fallback → error, no toolchain found. Fails.

go vs toolchain: go line = minimum required version, mandatory since Go 1.21; sets language version; must be ≥ dependency go lines. toolchain = suggested toolchain, only takes effect when module is main module and default toolchain older. Dependency's toolchain line is not read by consumers (only main module's); a dependency's go line, though, propagates: commands like go get raise main module go line when adding dependency requiring newer version — that can effectively bump consumers' requirements.

GOSUMDB=off: doesn't make automatic downloads work — it makes them fail: "toolchain downloads fail for lack of verification if GOSUMDB=off." Correct claim: GOSUMDB=off prevents toolchain downloads entirely. So the proposal is wrong even directionally. Recommend GOPROXY (e.g., mirror like a private proxy that serves golang.org/toolchain) instead; toolchain downloads can be proxied.

+path network-free: +path only disables download fallback for the selected toolchain; but other module downloads (dependencies) still may use network unless GOPROXY=off/module cache populated; also if a dependency requires newer toolchain and GOTOOLCHAIN is auto/path form, switching occurs — path form scans PATH. So +path alone does not make the whole build network-free; the build still fetches dependencies.

Guarantees not established: pinning toolchain line doesn't guarantee consumers use it (only main-module effect); go line sets language version but doesn't guarantee a patched compiler version; GOTOOLCHAIN settings don't guarantee reproducibility of toolchain across runners; no guarantee the toolchain line's specific patch version is used by downstream (they use bundled if newer... actually toolchain line takes effect only if default older). Also GOPRIVATE/GONOSUMDB don't apply to toolchain downloads. Verification of downloaded toolchains via checksum DB documented; GOPROXY + GOSUMDB can be kept.

Policy recommendation: publish modules with go line = minimum required (low), optionally toolchain line for local dev preference; pin CI exporters with GOTOOLCHAIN=<explicit version> or local with bundled version matching go line; for restricted network CI, prepopulate module cache with toolchain module or set GOPROXY to internal proxy that serves golang.org/toolchain, keep GOSUMDB on. Don't set GOSUMDB=off.

Keep under 400 words. Cite URLs with anchors.
